description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census.

`Test::More::subtest` is not implemented.  PCL's TAP layer (`cl/pcl-test.lisp`)
exports ok/is/like/cmp_ok/is_deeply/â¦ but not `subtest`, so a file that uses it
dies at the first call:

    Undefined subroutine &main::subtest called

and produces NO TAP AT ALL â the whole file, not the subtest.  On the board
that is Mojo-DOM58 t/collection.t, FAIL 0/0 where perl gives 20 rows.

REPRODUCE:
    tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Mojo-DOM58-3.002-0 t/collection.t
and minimally:
    use Test::More tests => 2;
    subtest 'inner' => sub { plan tests => 1; ok(1, 'a') };
    ok(1, 'outer');

WHAT IT IS: a subtest runs a code ref with a NESTED TAP stream â its own plan
and numbering, indented by four spaces, and the whole thing reported to the
parent as ONE `ok N - <name>` row.  Test::More's own rules that matter here:
the child's plan may be declared inside the block (`plan tests => N`) or
implied by `done_testing`; a child failure makes the parent row fail; the
child's diagnostics are indented with it; `subtest` returns the child's pass
verdict.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: `subtest` is how modern CPAN test files are written, so
its absence is not one board row â it is a whole style of test file producing
zero rows.  It is also self-contained: one function in `cl/pcl-test.lisp`
plus the indentation of the nested stream (the TAP layer already owns its
output through `%tap-out`), with `docs/tap-assertion-audit.md`'s rule applying
â a claim that cannot be evaluated reports `not ok` naming the reason, and only
`plan()` dies.

Guard: rows in `Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t` beside the existing plan/verdict rows.
